results.content: Training with contact mode labels substantially improves instruction-following grasp generation, especially for part grasp accuracy and contact mode compliance. The proposed model (DexVLG) benefits most from these labels, achieving the highest overall performance on the LVIS-Seen benchmark in simulation. Adding contact mode labels markedly boosts part grasp accuracy and contact mode accuracy across models. DexVLG with contact labels outperforms both its unlabeled counterpart and a baseline similarly augmented, showing the largest gains in part grasp compliance. Models without contact labels struggle to follow the extra finger-contact instruction, leading to degraded performance. [...] Training with explicit language instruction improves grasp success rates across all benchmarks and enables part-level accuracy evaluation. The largest gains occur for unseen objects, indicating better generalization when instructions are provided. Adding language instruction increases success rates on all benchmarks, with the most substantial improvement for unseen objects. Without instruction, part grasp accuracy is not reported, highlighting that language input is essential for part-level evaluation. [...] All final poses are validated in the IsaacGym physics simulator. A grasp is kept only if it meets four criteria: no hand-object penetration, no hand self-penetration, stability against gravity in all six axis-aligned directions during simulation, and part alignment where every contacting hand link is closer to the intended part than to any other part.
